<old lines, copied exactly>
'''.lstrip("\n")
new = r'''
<new lines>
'''.lstrip("\n")

Create new functions, parameters, messages or files with exactly the names the issue implies. Apply the same fix to an obvious sibling (both branches of a condition, load and loads) with one more edit.
4. Check. 5. Submit. Call the submit_patch tool once the targeted check passes, or once you have made the best change you can and 20 tool calls or most of the time are spent. Then reply with one sentence and stop.

import re
import sys
from datetime import date

RELEASE_NOTES_FILE = "docs/en/docs/release-notes.md"
RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\s*(\(.*\))?\s*$")


def main() -> None:
    with open(RELEASE_NOTES_FILE) as f:
        lines = f.readlines()

    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)
        if not match:
            continue

        version = match.group(1)
        date_part = match.group(2)

        if date_part:
            print(f"Latest release {version} already has a date: {date_part}")
            sys.exit(0)

        today = date.today().isoformat()
        lines[i] = f"## {version} ({today})\n"
        print(f"Added date: {version} ({today})")

        with open(RELEASE_NOTES_FILE, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
        sys.exit(0)

    print("No release header found")
    sys.exit(1)
